setup: Write the system as \(A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}\) with \(A = \begin{pmatrix} [[a]] & [[b]] \\ [[c]] & [[d]] \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\mathbf{b} = ([[e1]], [[e2]])\); a nonzero determinant means one solution, \(\mathbf{x} = A^{-1}\mathbf{b}\).

steps.say: The determinant of \(A\): \([[a_p]]\cdot [[d_p]] - [[b_p]]\cdot [[c_p]] = [[det]]\), which is not zero.

Cramer's rule for \(x\): replace the first column of \(A\) by \(\mathbf{b}\) and take the determinant, \([[e1_p]]\cdot [[d_p]] - [[b_p]]\cdot [[e2_p]] = [[detx]]\), so \(x = [[detx]]/[[det_p]] = [[x]]\).
And for \(y\): replace the second column, \([[a_p]]\cdot [[e2_p]] - [[e1_p]]\cdot [[c_p]] = [[dety]]\), so \(y = [[dety]]/[[det_p]] = [[y]]\).
